chapter: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
title: Why Danny could quit when Milt stayed until Cab's band broke up
summary: Milt says Danny had the nerve to quit the best-paid band, whereas Milt stayed until it folded, and Danny then took him to a Hoboken gig.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: But you had something that didn't nobody have, Danny. You knew how to get it. Like, you walked out... You were the only man I know that had enough nerve to quit that band. At that time, that was the highest-paid band in the country. Duke wasn't paying no more money than Cab was paying.
And for a man to just quit it... And we worked fifty weeks a year. And for a man to quit it, you got to be either crazy or you just got the strong fortitude of your convictions.

Which is, of course, what Danny had. He knew that he could make it regardless. Like, he just said here the other night, just give him a slice of bread and he'll make it. So if he didn't agree to whatever the principle was at that particular place, he would abdicate it -- he would leave it. Because I stayed there until the thing went right down. I didn't quit Cab's band.
The band broke up around me.

And there I was out there floundering around, and there Danny Barker was in New York, and he said, "What you doin'?" And I said "Nothing." And he said, "Well, come with me." And then what do you do? I took my bass and he took his guitar, and we got on the subway, and I wound up in Hoboken, New Jersey, with Danny Barker, and he says, "Come on with me..." Tell him about it, Danny.
